⚔️ The countries that won the most major battles — 1500 → 2003.

For centuries, ancient Rome's 55 victories stay the record. France draws level in 1745, pulls ahead two years later and never gives the lead back 🇫🇷 The engine is three centuries of almost constant European war, and above all Napoleon: France adds 82 wins between 1800 and 1815 alone. Then comes Waterloo. Winning battles is not the same as winning wars.

📊 Data: Historical Conflict Event Dataset (C. Miller & K. S. Bakar, Journal of Conflict Resolution, 2022), based on T. Jaques' Dictionary of Battles and Sieges, Harvard Dataverse, CC0. Only major battles count (3+ on the 1–6 Lehmann-Zhukov scale); many battles in the dataset carry no scale and are left out. A coalition win counts for every member, civil-war battles for no one, and historical states are credited to today's country (Prussia → Germany, England → UK).
